title: Cold rebuild: save a copy, keep the original
summary: Write a change to a new file and leave Vim without touching the original, in real Vim, from memory.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *Getting out* you wrote a change to a new file and left real Vim without touching
the original. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks are
exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. If you get stuck, go back to the lesson, then try
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: You typed `:q` and vim says `E37: No write since last change (add ! to override)`. You want to keep the file as it was on disk. What now?
steps.explain: `!` forces the quit and discards the edits. `:wq` would save the mess you wanted to throw away.

steps.title: Save a copy, keep the original, cold
prompt: `~/conf/app.conf` is live. With Vim (`vim -es` and `-c` commands), change `listen 80;` to `listen 8080;` and write the result to `~/conf/app.conf.new`.
The original must not change, and Vim must exit cleanly. From memory: no hints this time.
